name: deck_haiku
description: A haiku for the deck (PLAN O.4e, ADR-0030), about `topic`, the slide `slide` shows, or the whole talk. It calls no model. Without `lines`, it answers what to ask: the instructions and the prompt, in the deck's language, and how lines are counted; write the poem as asked. With `lines`, it counts them against 5, 7, and 5 (the engine counts English syllables and Japanese morae) and places them in one patch: on a new Haiku slide after `after` (else after `slide`, else the last), in `on`'s empty verse place, or over the verse text `replace`. The slide's notes say which model wrote it (`model`, else this client), when, and about what; nothing on the slide does. A poem off 5-7-5 is placed all the same: ask once more first.

bundle.description: The bundle: a directory, a `.scaena` zip, or a `deck.json`.

topic.description: What the haiku is about. Without it, the slide `slide` names, else the whole talk.

slide.description: The state whose slide the haiku is about.

lang.description: The language it is written in (BCP 47); else the deck's.

lines.description:
The poem, a line each: given, it is counted and placed; without it, the tool answers what
to ask.

after.description:
Put it on a new Haiku slide after this state's slide (the default: after `slide`, else after
the last).

on.description: Put it in this state's slide's empty verse place.

replace.description: Put it over this verse text, the looks of the words it keeps kept.

attribution.description: Who wrote it, or what it is on, set under it; never filled in for the person.

model.description: The model that wrote the lines, which the slide's notes name; else the client.

date.description: The day it was written, as the notes say it (`October 15, 2026`); else this machine's.

dry_run.description: Say what it would write, and write nothing.

Patched.description: What a patch did, or would do.

applied.description: Whether the deck was written: not under a dry run, nor when the patch was refused.

patch.description: The patch as RFC 6902, in order.

added.description: What `validate` and `lint` find after the patch that they did not before.

removed.description: What they found before that they do not after.

errors.description: The findings that are errors, after.

states.description:
The states it changes, by id: each whose nodes, resolved with the deck's overrides,
or whose layout, transition, choreography, hold, notes, or slide number and footer are
not as they were, and each it adds. None when it is refused.

oneOf.description:
Put `value` at `path`: a member of an object (one already there is replaced, in its
place), or an item of an array, at an index or at its end (`-`).
Replace what is at `path`, which must be there.

`remove` at `from`, then `add` at `path`. A member moved within its object keeps its
place: a rename.
Fail the patch unless `path` holds `value` (numbers equal by value: 1 is 1.0).

Pointer.description:
A JSON Pointer (RFC 6901): empty, the whole document, or `/`-separated tokens, `~1` for a
`/` and `~0` for a `~` inside one.

Finding.description: One lint finding, shaped for agents: a code, a JSON pointer, and (when safe) a fix.

file.description: The bundle file `path` points into, when it is not `deck.json` (a theme file).

format.description: The format the deck was laid out in (`"9:16"`), when it is not the deck's own.

fix.description: A JSON Patch (RFC 6902) that resolves the finding. Only safe, non-content fixes.

refresh.description:
The data source to fetch again, where what resolves the finding is a fetch, which no patch
makes (W428, ADR-0030): the source's name, without its `@`.

instructions.description: What the model is told it does.

lang.description: The language it is asked in, BCP 47.

about.description: What the haiku is about, as its slide's notes will say it.

counted.description: How its lines are counted: syllables, morae, or not at all.

counts.description: Each line's count, a range where it may be said two ways; none where it is uncounted.

state.description: The state it is on, and its text node.
